newsitem.title: UK: RJB Mining profit rises, ups dividend.
newsitem.headline: RJB Mining profit rises, ups dividend.

text.p: RJB Mining Plc, which owns much of the formerly state-run English coal fields, on Tuesday reported a 9.3 percent rise in 1996 profits, while raising its its dividend by 25 percent.

Ongoing cost-cutting helped lift pre-tax profit to a better-than-expected 189.2 million pounds from 173.1 million the previous year. The dividend was increased to 20.0 pence per share from 16.0 pence.
"During the year the company has continued to reduce costs and has progressed the restructuring of the business to improve further competitiveness," said chief executive Richard Budge.
RJB, which on Monday announced it might build a "clean coal" power station with National Power Plc and Texaco Inc, said it had increased its share in both the domestic and industrial coal market.
RJB's core underground mining operations produced 27.7 million tonnes of coal last year, down from 29.9 million in 1995.
Production at the opencast mines, which make up 20 percent of total output, remained unchanged at 7.2 million tonnes.
